Rashi on Chullin 80a:11:1.hebrew: בריה בפני עצמה - ולא מכלאי בהמה וחיה הוא בא, דס"ל אין חיה מתעברת מבהמה ולא בהמה מחיה, וה"נ אמרינן בב"ק (דף עח.). ומיהו רב יהודה לאו אליבא דר' אליעזר ורבנן נקט מילתא, דאינהו ודאי סבירא להו דמכלאי בהמה וחיה הוא בא, והכי נמי אמרינן בב"ק: "חוץ מרבי אליעזר ומחלוקתו שהיו אומרים חיה מתעברת מבהמה":
Rashi on Chullin 80a:11:1.english: A distinct entity - And it does not come from the crossbreeding of a domesticated animal and an undomesticated animal, for he holds [that] an undomesticated animal cannot conceive from a domesticated animal, nor a domesticated animal from an undomesticated animal — and so too we say in Bava Kamma (78a). However, Rav Yehuda did not state [his] teaching in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer and the Rabbis, for they certainly hold that it comes from the crossbreeding of a domesticated animal and an undomesticated animal; and so too we say in Bava Kamma: "Except for Rabbi Eliezer and his disputants, who would say [that] an undomesticated animal can conceive from a domesticated animal":

Rashi on Chullin 80a:11:2.english: The wild ram - A male ram that grows in the forests:

Rashi on Chullin 80a:12:1.english: The house of Dushai - [This is] a family named after its ancestor:

Rashi on Chullin 80a:13:1.english: Goats of bala - Goats of Lebanon. Bala [means] forest:

Rashi on Chullin 80a:13:2.english: [They are] fit for the altar - For they are not undomesticated animals, but domesticated animals:

Rashi on Chullin 80a:13:3.hebrew: עשר בהמות מנה הכתוב - להיתר אכילה: "שור שה כשבים ושה עזים איל וצבי ויחמור ואקו ודישון ותאו וזמר" (דברים יד), ואין לנו עוד בהמה וחיה כשרה בעולם. והשתא להנהו עזי דבאלא ליכא לספוקי שמא מין חיה הוא שלא הוזכרה כאן, דהא תו ליכא; ומדלא מנינהו להנך בהדי חיות, ש"מ בכלל עז הן, ועז בהמה הוא:
Rashi on Chullin 80a:13:3.english: The verse lists ten animals - for permissibility of eating: "An ox, a seh of sheep, and a seh of goats, a deer, and a gazelle, and a fallow deer, and a wild goat, and an oryx, and an aurochs, and a wild sheep" (Deuteronomy 14), and we have no other kosher domesticated or wild animal in the world. And now, regarding these forest goats, there is no room for doubt that perhaps it is a species of wild animal that was not mentioned here, for there are no more [species]. And since [the verse] did not list them among the wild animals, learn from this [that] they are included under [the category of] "goat," and a goat is a domesticated animal:

Rashi on Chullin 80a:14:1.hebrew: מתקיף לה רב אחא - נהי נמי דאין עוד מין חיה שלא הוזכרה כאן, אכתי מנא לך דמינא דעז הוא? דלמא מינא דאקו נינהו, ולא ידעינן מאי ניהו, או תאו או זמר — הנך דלא בקיאינן בהו — ודלמא הני נינהו:
Rashi on Chullin 80a:14:1.english: Rav Aḥa objects to this - Even though there is no other species of undomesticated animal that was not mentioned here [in the verse], still, from where do you [know] that it is a species of goat? Perhaps they are a species of akko — and we do not know what it is — or te'o, or zemer — those [animals] with which we are not familiar — and perhaps these [forest goats] are those:

Rashi on Chullin 80a:17:1.hebrew: שרי תרבייהו - לאכילה, דס"ל חיות נינהו:
Rashi on Chullin 80a:17:1.english: Permits their fat - for eating, because he holds [that] they are undomesticated animals:

Rashi on Chullin 80a:19:1.english: Teo [“aurochs”], we translate [as] turbala - [meaning] the ox of Lebanon:

Rashi on Chullin 80a:19:2.hebrew: אבל הני - דלא מנינהו בהדי חיות, דברי הכל מין עז נינהו:
Rashi on Chullin 80a:19:2.english: But these - since [Scripture] did not enumerate them among the undomesticated animals, all agree [that] they are a species of goat:

Rashi on Chullin 80a:1:1.english: [They disagree] concerning "sheep," [whether it includes] even partially a sheep - [This is] as Rav Pappa goes on to explain:

Rashi on Chullin 80a:21:1.hebrew: ר"ש שמעינן ליה - במתניתין (לקמן חולין דף פא:) דאמר שחיטה שאינה ראויה לא שמה שחיטה, ולא מחייב עליה משום אותו ואת בנו, דקתני: ר' שמעון פוטר בשוחט שור הנסקל:
Rashi on Chullin 80a:21:1.english: We have heard [that] Rabbi Shimon - in the Mishnah (below, Chullin 81b), [says that] an act of slaughter that is unfit [is] not considered [an act of] slaughter, and one is not liable for it on account of [the prohibition of] an animal and its offspring, as [the Mishnah] teaches: Rabbi Shimon exempts one who slaughters an ox [that was sentenced] to be stoned:

Rashi on Chullin 80a:2:1.hebrew: הילכך לענין כסוי הדם כו' - כלומר, הואיל ואוקימנא דלתרוייהו מספקא להו, וב"שה ואפילו מקצת שה" פליגי:
Rashi on Chullin 80a:2:1.english: Therefore, with regard to the matter of covering the blood, etc. - That is to say, since we have established that both of them are in doubt [as to its status], and they disagree regarding [whether] "a sheep" [includes] even part of a sheep:

Rashi on Chullin 80a:2:2.hebrew: לענין כסוי הדם - דקתני "אין שוחטין", דמשמע: ודאי חייב בכסוי, ספק פטור; ולענין מתנות דפליגי בה:
Rashi on Chullin 80a:2:2.english: With regard to the matter of covering the blood - as [the Mishnah] teaches: "One may not slaughter [it on a Festival]," which implies [that if it is] definitely obligated in covering [the blood, one may slaughter it, whereas if it is] uncertain, it is exempt [from covering on a Festival]; and with regard to the [priestly] gifts, about which they disagree:

Rashi on Chullin 80a:2:3.hebrew: לא משכחת לה אלא בצבי הבא על התיישה וכו' - והא דקתני "אין שוחטין", רבנן היא; ומשום שמא חוששין, וחייב בכסוי, דאית להו "צבי" ואפי' מקצת צבי, ושמא אין חוששין, ופטור מן הכסוי, דאפילו מקצת צבי ליכא. דבתייש הבא על הצבייה ליכא לאוקומה דתיתוקם כרבנן, דהא ודאי איכא מקצת צבי, ולישחוט וליכסי לרבנן. ולרבי אליעזר ודאי הוה מצי לאוקמא בתייש הבא על הצבייה: שמא חוששין וליכא אלא מקצת צבי, ומקצת לית ליה, ושמא אין חוששין וכוליה צבי הוא ובעי כסוי; אבל ניחא ליה לאוקמא כדרבנן. ולעלין מתנות נמי, בצבי הבא על התיישה: ולר"א פטור לגמרי, דשמא חוששין וליכא אלא מקצת שה דאם, ו"שה" ואפי' מקצת שה לית ליה; וכיון דמספקא לן, המוציא מחבירו עליו הראיה, וא"ל: אייתי ראיה דאין חוששין וכוליה שה הוא, ושקול. ולרבנן, חייב מיהא בחצי מתנות ממה נפשך: דאי אין חוששין — כוליה שה הוא, ואי חוששין — מקצת שיות דאם מיהא איכא, ורבנן אית להו "שה" ואפילו מקצת שה; ושקיל פלגא דשיות, ואידך פלגא אימא ליה: אייתי ראיה דאין חוששין וכוליה שה הוא, ושקול. ובתייש הבא על הצבייה ליכא לאוקומיה, דא"כ לרבנן נמי ליפטר: דנהי נמי דאפי' מקצת שה אמרינן, מי לימא לן דאיכא מקצת שה? דלמא אין חוששין וכוליה צבי הוא — המוציא מחבירו עליו הראיה:
Rashi on Chullin 80a:2:3.english: You find it only in [the case of] a deer that mated with a female goat, etc. - And that which [the Mishnah] teaches, "one may not slaughter [it on a festival]," is [the view of] the Rabbis; and [it is] because perhaps we are concerned [for the father's seed], and [thus] it is obligated in covering [the blood], since they hold [that] "deer" [includes] even a partial deer, and perhaps we are not concerned [for the father's seed], and [thus] it is exempt from covering [the blood], since there is not even a partial deer [in it]. For in [the case of] a male goat that mated with a female deer, it is impossible to establish it so that it is established according to the Rabbis, because there is certainly a partial deer [in it], so let one slaughter [it on a festival] and cover [its blood] according to the Rabbis! And according to Rabbi Eliezer, he [Rav Pappa] certainly could have established it in [the case of] a male goat that mated with a female deer: perhaps we are concerned [for the father's seed] and there is only a partial deer, and he does not hold [that "deer" includes] a partial [deer]; and perhaps we are not concerned [for the father's seed] and it is entirely a deer and requires covering [the blood] — however, it was preferable to him to establish it according to the Rabbis. And regarding the [priestly] gifts as well, [it is established] in [the case of] a deer that mated with a female goat: according to Rabbi Eliezer, he is completely exempt, for perhaps we are concerned [for the father's seed] and there is only a partial lamb from the mother, and [he holds that] "lamb" [does] not [include] even a partial lamb; and since we are in doubt, [the rule is] "the burden of proof is upon the one who seeks to exact [property] from his fellow," and he [the owner] says to him [the Kohen], "Bring proof that we are not concerned [for the father's seed] and it is entirely a lamb, and take [it]." And according to the Rabbis, he is obligated at least in half the gifts either way: for if we are not concerned [for the father's seed] — it is entirely a lamb, and if we are concerned [for the father's seed] — there is at least a partial lamb-ness from the mother, and the Rabbis hold [that] "lamb" [includes] even a partial lamb; so he [the Kohen] takes half [for] the lamb-ness, and [for] the other half he says to him, "Bring proof that we are not concerned [for the father's seed] and it is entirely a lamb, and take [it]." And in [the case of] a male goat that mated with a female deer, it is impossible to establish it, because if so, according to the Rabbis too he should be exempt: for even though we say [that "lamb" includes] even a partial lamb, who can tell us that there is a partial lamb [here]? Perhaps we are not concerned [for the father's seed] and it is entirely a deer — "the burden of proof is upon the one who seeks to exact [property] from his fellow":

Rashi on Chullin 80a:5:1.hebrew: לענין אותו ואת בנו משכחת לה - לפלוגתייהו דלעיל, בין בתייש כו':
Rashi on Chullin 80a:5:1.english: With regard to itself and its offspring, you find it - [Referring to] their dispute above, whether with a he-goat, etc.:

Rashi on Chullin 80a:6:1.hebrew: בתייש הבא על הצבייה ולאיסורא - בעלמא קאמרי רבנן דנוהג, ואסור לשוחטה לנקבה הבאה מן התייש והצבייה עם בנה, משום שמא חוששין ואיכא מקצת שה, ורבנן אית להו מקצת שה. אבל מלקות ליכא, דשמא אין חוששין ואפילו מקצת שה ליכא, הילכך הויא לה התראת ספק ולא שמה התראה, ואין מלקות בלא התראה. ולר"א מותר לכתחלה, דא"נ חוששין ואיכא מקצת שה, לית ליה מקצת שה:
Rashi on Chullin 80a:6:1.english: With a he-goat that mates with a doe, and [it relates] to a prohibition - merely [as a prohibition] the Rabbis say that it applies, and it is prohibited to slaughter the female [offspring] born from the he-goat and the doe together with its offspring, because perhaps one is concerned [with the father's seed] and there is a partial seh [sheep or goat], and the Rabbis hold [that the verse includes] a partial seh. However, there are no lashes, because perhaps one is not concerned [with the father's seed] and there is not even a partial seh; therefore, it is a doubtful warning, and [a doubtful warning] is not considered a [valid] warning, and there are no lashes without a [valid] warning. And according to Rabbi Eliezer, it is permitted ab initio, for even if one is concerned [with the father's seed] and there is a partial seh, he does not hold [that the verse includes] a partial seh:

Rashi on Chullin 80a:7:1.english: Even though we are concerned - [nevertheless,] there is a partial sheep of the mother:

Tosafot on Chullin 80a:11:1.hebrew: כוי בריה בפני עצמה היא - אמתניתין דכסוי הדם (לקמן חולין פג:) קאי, דתנן: ונוהג בכוי מפני שהוא ספק, ואין שוחטין אותו בי"ט, ואם שחטו כו'; ולא אכוי שנחלקו בו ר' אליעזר ורבנן קאי, כדפירש בקונטרס:
Tosafot on Chullin 80a:11:1.english: A koy is a distinct entity - [Rav Yehuda] refers to the Mishnah of Covering the Blood (below, Chullin 83b), where we learned: "[The mitzva] applies to a koy because it is [a matter of] uncertainty, and one may not slaughter it on a Festival, and if one slaughtered it, etc."; and he does not refer to the koy concerning which Rabbi Eliezer and the Rabbis disagreed, as Rashi explained:

Tosafot on Chullin 80a:11:2.hebrew: ולא הכריעו בו חכמים אם מין בהמה או מין חיה - וא"ת: ולבדוק בסימנין דקרנים? וי"ל, דאפשר דלא היו יכולין לברר בקרניו שפיר אם חדודות וכרוכות יפה:
Tosafot on Chullin 80a:11:2.english: And the Sages did not determine regarding it whether [it is] a species of domesticated animal or a species of undomesticated animal - And if you ask: Let them check by the signs of the horns? And one can answer that perhaps they were not able to ascertain well from its horns whether [they are] pointed and ringed properly:

Tosafot on Chullin 80a:11:3.hebrew: זה איל הבר - וסבר רב נחמן ות"ק דברייתא שהוא ודאי חיה, ושוחטים אותו בי"ט ומכסין דמו, ופליגי אמתניתין (לקמן חולין דף פג:). אבל אין לומר דלדידהו בהמה הוה, דאם כן ת"ק היינו רשב"ג:
Tosafot on Chullin 80a:11:3.english: This is the wild ram - And Rav Naḥman and the first tanna of the baraita hold that it is definitely an undomesticated animal, and [therefore] one may slaughter it on a Festival and cover its blood, and they disagree with our Mishnah (below, Chullin 83b). However, one cannot say that according to them it is a domesticated animal, for if so, [the opinion of] the first tanna would be [the same as] Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel:

Tosafot on Chullin 80a:19:1.hebrew: מדחשיב ליה בהדי חיות ש"מ דחיה הוא - משמע דאי לאו דחשיב ליה בהדי חיות, הוי בהמה לכ"ע, משום דנקרא שור. וקשה קצת, דאיל הבר הוי חיה כדפי' לעיל, אף על גב דנקרא איל:
Tosafot on Chullin 80a:19:1.english: Since it reckons it among the undomesticated animals, learn from this that it is an undomesticated animal - This implies that were it not that it reckons it among the undomesticated animals, it would be [considered] a domesticated animal according to everyone, because it is called an ox. And this is somewhat difficult, for the wild ram is an undomesticated animal, as I explained above, even though it is called a ram:

Tosafot on Chullin 80a:20:1.hebrew: ודלמא מינא דתאו הוא - וקסבר רב אחא דתאו מין חיה הוא, כרבי יוסי דאמר בסמוך: שור הבר מין חיה; דאי כרבנן דאמרי מין בהמה הוא, א"כ כי הוי נמי מין תאו, הוי כשר לגבי מזבח:
Tosafot on Chullin 80a:20:1.english: But perhaps it is a type of aurochs - And Rav Aḥa holds that the aurochs is a species of wild animal, in accordance with Rabbi Yosei, who says shortly [hereafter]: The wild ox is a species of wild animal. For if [he held] in accordance with the Rabbis, who say it is a species of domesticated animal, then even if it were a type of aurochs, it would be fit for the altar:

Tosafot on Chullin 80a:21:1.hebrew: חולין בחוץ שניהם כשרים - ס"ד דמיפסל שני משום "לא תאכל כל תועבה", כדאמר בפרק כל הבשר (לקמן חולין דף קטו.):
Tosafot on Chullin 80a:21:1.english: Non-sacred [animals slaughtered] outside [the Temple], both are fit - You might have thought that the second [animal] is disqualified because of [the verse,] "You shall not eat any abominable thing," as [the Gemara] says in the chapter [entitled] Kol HaBasar (below, Chullin 115a):

Tosafot on Chullin 80a:21:2.hebrew: הראשון חייב כרת ושניהם סופגין את הארבעים - דלא כר' יצחק אתיא, דאמר בפרק אלו הן הלוקין (מכות דף כג.): חייבי כריתות שלקו, נפטרו מידי כריתתם. ועוד הוה מצי למתני: חולין וקדשים בחוץ ובפנים, וכן קדשים וחולין; וחולין וקדשים בפנים ובחוץ, וכן קדשים וחולין. ואי בכל הני דתני יש חדוש, איכא למימר דלא תנא להני משום דליכא בהו שום חדוש; ואי ליכא חדוש בכל הני דתני, צ"ל "תני ושייר":
Tosafot on Chullin 80a:21:2.english: The first is liable to karet, and both of them incur forty [lashes] - [This] follows not in accordance with Rabbi Yitzchak, who says in the chapter [entitled] Eilu Hen HaLokin (Makkot 23a): Those liable to karet who received lashes are exempted from their karet. And furthermore, [the Mishnah] could have taught [the cases of] non-sacrificial and sacrificial [animals slaughtered] outside and inside [the Temple courtyard, respectively], and similarly sacrificial and non-sacrificial [animals]; and non-sacrificial and sacrificial [animals slaughtered] inside and outside, and similarly sacrificial and non-sacrificial [animals]. And if in all these [cases] that [the Mishnah] taught there is a novelty, one can say that it did not teach these [additional cases] because there is no novelty in them; and if there is no novelty in all these [cases] that it taught, one must say "[the Tanna] taught [some] and omitted [others]":
